Date: 2028-05-14T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick root-cause notes (batching/queue depth)

Internal note (do not forward directly):

Observed behavior: sudden spike in short, chatty parallel requests from a small subset of keys producing a large increase in queue depth. Continuous batching heuristics increased aggregate batch sizes during the brief throughput surge; however our new batching-threshold optimizer (rolled last week) misclassified the traffic as "steady-state" and allowed larger batch windows to persist, which amplified tail latency when requests briefly aborted/errored and left inflight KV cache contention. That produced cascading retries and a backlog.

Evidence: ops_logs_snippet_20280514.txt shows queue depth jumping from 40->280 in ~90s on the us-west serving pool. Kernel busy time increased and the p99 stepped up as batch completion latency multiplied.

Temporary mitigation recommended (fast):
- Override continuous_batching.window_ms for KiteHealth org -> set from 50ms down to 10ms (reduces batching aggregation).
- Reduce org max_concurrency from 48 -> 20 for the next 30 minutes.
- Enable fallback routing to the dedicated-cpu-backup variant for non-critical /embed requests.

Longer-term fixes: rollback the recent optimizer change that auto-extended windows for mixed short/long request patterns; add prefix-aware batching and KV cache eviction heuristics.

I'll apply the overrides if Marcus gives the green light; we should prepare a short customer note describing root cause and the mitigation timeline.

Steph
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-14T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick root-cause notes (batching/queue depth)

Confirmed. Queue metrics attached and I've applied the temporary overrides: continuous_batching.window_ms=10ms for org=KiteHealth, org_max_concurrency=20. Routing rule flipped for non-critical paths to dedicated-cpu-backup.

Initial impact: p95 has dropped from ~2.4s to ~380ms within 4 minutes; p99 still at ~1.2s but trending down. Error rate (502) reduced by ~70%. Monitoring on anomaly thresholds for the next hour.

I'll keep the override in place and start a controlled ramp of concurrency if the bridge agrees. We'll prepare a postmortem and proposed change set.

Marcus
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sharp latency/502 spike — summary and next steps

Alicia/Carlos — quick update: thanks for alerting us and for joining the bridge.

What we saw: a short traffic shape shift caused queue depth to jump on the us-west pool; a batching heuristic regression amplified aggregation which exposed a KV cache contention pattern and produced elevated p95/p99 and 502s.

What we did:
- Applied temporary overrides to reduce batching window and concurrency for KiteHealth (details below).
- Routed non-critical requests to a backup variant to lower the pressure on the main serving pool.
- Monitoring shows p95 improved from ~2.4s to ~380ms; error rate down ~70%.

Immediate ask from us: please avoid bulk replaying of historical traffic until we finish the postmortem and we confirm stable metrics.

Next steps and timeline:
- Today: keep mitigations for 2–4 hours while we validate.
- By EOD PST: postmortem draft and permanent fix plan (rollback of batching optimizer or tuned threshold).
- Credits: we'll propose a pro-rated SLA credit commensurate with impact; I'll loop finance and legal and follow up by EOD.

Would you like a short exec note summarizing this for KiteHealth leadership? We can provide status updates and the postmortem link once ready.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously.

Logan Wright
Account Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec note for KiteHealth leadership (draft)

Team — drafting the exec note requested by KiteHealth VP. Please keep internal until we finalize:

Summary: On 2028-05-14 08:45–09:10 UTC we reported elevated p95/p99 and an increased 502 rate impacting customer checkout. Root cause: a recent batching-threshold optimizer mischaracterized a short traffic surge as steady-state and extended batch windows, which increased queue depth and amplified KV cache contention. This produced cascading retries and tail amplification.

Impact: ~23 minutes of degraded tail latency (p95 ~2.4s peak) and intermittent 502s; error rate reduced by ~70% after mitigations. Customers affected: KiteHealth (primary), small subset of other hosted API customers routed on the same us-west pool.

Mitigation taken: temporary overrides to batching window and org concurrency; routing of non-critical requests to backup variant. Metrics indicate service stabilized within ~10 minutes of overrides.

Follow-up: full postmortem and proposed permanent fix (rollback / retune of batching optimizer) to be delivered EOD. Finance to propose SLA credit; CS to coordinate customer-facing exec note.

Please comment with edits; I'll send the external version to Alicia once we agree.

Logan Wright
Account Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
